# Link

The text link, in both house treatments. default and muted are the standalone UI link for chrome, warming to the brand accent on hover; prose is the hyperlink embedded in running copy, underlined at rest.

```tsx
<Link href="#">hello@koalaui.com</Link>
<Link href="#" variant="muted">Documentation</Link>
<Link href="#" underline>Read the changelog</Link>
<Link href="#">Open in a new tab <ArrowUpRight /></Link>

<p className="text-muted-foreground">
  Read the <Link href="#" variant="prose">changelog</Link> before upgrading.
</p>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add link
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/link/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Link } from "@/components/ui/link"

export function Example() {
  return <Link href="/pricing">See pricing</Link>
}
```

## Variants

`default` rests at `text-foreground` (full-strength, reads as a real label); `muted` starts quiet for a value in a directory or a footer link. Both lift to the brand accent on hover. `prose` is the third treatment, for a link inside a sentence: it sets *no* rest color, so it inherits the copy around it, and only its underline marks it until hover turns both text and underline the accent.

```tsx
<Link href="#" variant="default">Full-strength link</Link>
<Link href="#" variant="muted">Muted link</Link>

{/* prose sets no rest color: it inherits whatever copy it sits in. */}
<p className="text-muted-foreground">Muted copy with a <Link href="#" variant="prose">prose link</Link>.</p>
<p className="text-foreground">Full-strength copy with a <Link href="#" variant="prose">prose link</Link>.</p>
```

## In prose

A hyperlink inside running copy is a different animal from a link in UI chrome, so `prose` is a treatment rather than a color: it inherits the paragraph's color, wears a hairline `decoration-border` underline at rest, and turns both the text and the underline the `--link` token on hover. It stays `display: inline` so it breaks across lines mid-sentence instead of wrapping as an unbreakable block, drops the trailing-icon reveal the standalone variants carry (a glyph in prose is content, not a hover affordance), and hovers on the faster 160ms beat, because a word-sized target in a paragraph is swept over constantly and a slow fade out leaves a trail of words cooling back down.

```tsx title="in-prose.tsx"
import NextLink from "next/link"
import { Link } from "@/components/ui/link"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <p className="text-muted-foreground">
      Components are owned source in your repo. Start with the{" "}
      {/* asChild keeps an internal prose link on client-side routing. */}
      <Link asChild variant="prose">
        <NextLink href="/docs/installation">installation guide</NextLink>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  )
}
```

## Underline

The color shift carries the affordance in context, so the link is not underlined by default. Pass `underline` for a prose-like link that must read as underlined at rest. It applies to `default` and `muted` only: `prose` is underlined by definition, and pinning a thickness on it (the prop sets `decoration-1`) would stop the underline tracking the font metrics, so combining the two is a type error.

```tsx
<Link href="#">No underline</Link>
<Link href="#" underline>Underlined at rest</Link>
```

## With an icon

Drop a trailing glyph (a directional arrow for an outbound or routing link) beside the label. It reads as a hover affordance, so it stays hidden at rest and slides and fades in when the link is hovered or keyboard-focused, warming to brand with the text. The motion is a plain CSS transition (interruptible), and it collapses to an instant reveal under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

```tsx
<Link href="#">View the docs <ArrowUpRight /></Link>
```

## As child

Use `asChild` to render the link styles onto another element, e.g. Next.js's `Link`, via Radix Slot, so you keep client-side routing.

```tsx title="as-child.tsx"
import NextLink from "next/link"
import { Link } from "@/components/ui/link"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Link asChild>
      <NextLink href="/pricing">See pricing</NextLink>
    </Link>
  )
}
```

## FAQ

### Which variant do I use?

Ask where the link sits. Outside running prose (a contact row, a directory card, a footer column, a meta row) use default, or muted when it should start quiet: both rest at a solid color and warm to brand on hover. Inside a sentence, use prose. Never hand-roll the classes: this component is the only place the treatment is defined.

### Why doesn't prose set a text color?

Because the paragraph already did. A hyperlink in running copy should read as part of its sentence, so prose inherits: text-muted-foreground inside a muted <p>, text-foreground inside a Pricing feature row. Only the hover state is colored, which is what makes that color mean something. Pass a text-* through className on the rare row that needs to override the copy around it.

### Why isn't it underlined by default?

That applies to default and muted only. Outside prose, these links sit in a labeled context (a value under a heading, a card, a footer column) where the layout already reads them as links, so the color shift on hover is enough affordance. Pass the underline prop when such a link needs to read as underlined at rest. prose is always underlined, since inside a sentence nothing else marks the link.

### How do I keep Next.js client-side routing?

Set asChild and pass a single next/link child. The Link renders its styles onto that element via Radix Slot instead of emitting its own <a>, so the navigation stays client-side.

### Does it re-theme and re-accent?

Yes. The rest color is text-foreground (or text-muted-foreground, or inherited under prose) and the hover is the brand accent, all semantic tokens, so it reads correctly in light, dark, cream, and moonlight and re-tints with the active accent. prose hovers to --link, which derives from --brand and so carries the accent too. It stays a separate role because it is tuned for text: on light it is darkened to clear the 4.5:1 AA floor the raw accent misses at 3.6:1, while the dark themes use the accent straight.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add link` writes `components/ui/link/`. Import from `@/components/ui/link`:

- Components and helpers: `Link`, `linkVariants`
- Types: `LinkProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `tv`
- npm packages: `radix-ui`
